rows.subtype: Approach: watching others and copying their arm strokes [Action]
rows.description: A boy watches an older swimmer's arm movement and copies it on the poolside. He tries it in the water with the coach watching, who fixes his elbow position.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: emotion-aware planning, trial by imitation

rows.subtype: Approach: practising only with a float and never without [Pitfall]
rows.description: A girl always holds a kickboard because it feels safe. After weeks she still cannot swim alone, since she never tried letting go even in the shallow water with the coach nearby.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, emotion-aware planning, trial by imitation

rows.subtype: Approach: swimming only when a trained adult is watching [Thinking]
rows.description: A child understands that pools and rivers can be dangerous and decides never to go into water without a grown-up lifeguard. He treats this as part of the plan, not a limit.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, emotion-aware planning

rows.subtype: Approach: setting small distances as goals [Revision]
rows.description: Feeling slow, a girl decides to swim one width of the pool, then two. Each goal is small enough to reach, and she counts her progress in widths each week.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, emotion-aware planning, trial by imitation

rows.subtype: Approach: writing a list from the teacher's notice [Action]
rows.description: A boy reads the circular for the museum trip and lists lunch, water, cap, ID card and money. Using the notice as the source means he does not have to guess.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: learning from past failure, mental simulation, pre-mortem

rows.subtype: Approach: imagining the day from morning to evening [Thinking]
rows.description: A girl walks through the trip in her mind, the bus, walking in the sun, lunch, and the ride back. She adds a hat, tissues and a plastic bag for wrappers.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: learning from past failure, pre-mortem

rows.subtype: Approach: packing at the last minute in a hurry [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child begins packing at 6:30 am when the bus is due at 7. He forgets his permission slip and water bottle, and his mother has to run to the gate with them.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: learning from past failure, mental simulation, pre-mortem

rows.subtype: Approach: keeping the bag light and taking only what is needed [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy remembers a heavy bag tired him last time. He decides to leave out toys and extra books, and picks a small bag that he can carry all day.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: mental simulation, pre-mortem

rows.subtype: Approach: packing the day before and checking twice [Action]
rows.description: A girl packs the evening before and checks the list again in the morning. The two checks catch the missing sun cap, and she goes with a calm mind.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: learning from past failure, mental simulation, pre-mortem

rows.subtype: Approach: taking everything he might possibly need [Pitfall]
rows.description: A boy is so worried about what could go wrong that he packs three snacks, two jackets and a big torch. The bag is heavy and the teacher asks him to leave half at school.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: learning from past failure, mental simulation
